# Assess IPO readiness and public-company operations

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When the board considers whether a public listing could be an appropriate financing or liquidity route. A board-reviewed readiness and go-or-no-go decision with a specialist-owned execution and operating plan.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Define the objective and readiness baseline

agent-runnable


Record financing and liquidity goals, financial history, ownership, controls, product risks and management capacity. Distinguish a readiness assessment from launching an offering or promising a listing date.

- Sources: [SEC going public](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/going-public) · [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Select the market and qualified advisers

human · human approval required


The board and securities counsel assess suitable jurisdictions, venues, eligibility and alternatives. Appoint appropriately qualified financial, audit and legal advisers and confirm conflicts and engagement scope.

- Sources: [SEC going public](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/going-public) · [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Build the readiness gap and evidence register

agent-runnable


Reconcile audited financials, governance, equity, controls, disclosures and public-company reporting capability. Assign gaps and evidence owners and document assumptions that depend on the chosen market or transaction route.

- Sources: [SEC going public](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/going-public) · [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve remediation and ongoing operating capacity

human · human approval required


Leadership agrees the budget, governance changes, reporting controls and staffing needed before a launch decision. Qualified reviewers determine required filings, communications controls and approvals for the selected route.

- Sources: [SEC going public](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/going-public) · [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Decide whether to proceed and authorize the next stage

human · human approval required


The board reviews readiness, market conditions, costs and alternatives with advisers. Authorize a separately scoped transaction only when required, keeping any offering, disclosure or filing within its specialist-led approval process.

- Verify: A board-reviewed readiness and go-or-no-go decision with a specialist-owned execution and operating plan.
- Sources: [SEC going public](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/going-public) · [FRC small and medium-sized enterprises](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/smes/)
